observations: Transverse 4-cylinder car engine with plastic timing and valve covers.
Engine is sitting on a concrete floor in a workshop or spare parts yard.
White marker writing 'OK' and 'SOLD' is visible on the top plastic cover in photo 1.
Watermark 'CHIDO MOTOR' is superimposed on all three photos.
The engine appears to be a 'long block' assembly; major accessories like the alternator or AC compressor are not clearly visible.
A second engine and a person are visible in the background of photo 2.

claims.claim: Japanese parts such as Toyota Nissan Honda
claims.evidence: The engine design is consistent with Japanese manufacturers, but no brand logos are legible in the photos.
Handwritten marks on the casing are seller statements and do not constitute proof of mechanical functionality.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure (e.g., seized, blown head gasket)
risks.proof: A video of the engine running or a professional compression test result.

risks.risk: Missing essential bolt-on components (alternator, starter, AC compressor)
risks.proof: Clear photos of all sides of the engine assembly.
A clear photo of the engine model code stamped on the metal engine block.

proof_requests: Photo of the engine model code stamped on the metal engine block (e.g., 2AZ, 1ZZ, K24).
Close-up photo of any manufacturer logos or part number stickers.
Video of the engine being cranked or running.
Photos of the engine from all four sides to confirm which accessories are included.
response.reason: The specific engine model, which is the primary driver of value and compatibility, cannot be identified from the photos. Pricing a generic engine without a model is not possible as values vary significantly.
